Title: April 2, 2026 Boulder City Council Regular Meeting (Thursday evening session)
Overview: The council heard extensive open comment on the South Boulder Rec Center future, tipped wage credit, and open space, then approved a consent agenda (with Council Member Adams voting no on item 4E related to Area III) and adopted Ordinance 8743 on a unanimous 8-0 vote expanding festival lodging rental licenses to tenants with owner consent for Sundance. The council also began exploring local authority to modify the tip offset, straw-polling to remove option three and keep the status quo, 2A, 2B, and a Benjamin sunset proposal, with staff directed to return with timing details through CAC.

Topic1.Title: Open Comment: South Boulder Rec Center and Pool
Topic1.Summary: Many residents, including children and seniors, spoke in favor of preserving the South Boulder Rec Center pool, gym, and walkability for families. Speakers questioned the lack of a repair or cost analysis and the option of saving the existing building, while others urged prioritizing South Boulder in capital investment. Staff acknowledged the passion and said holistic facility data would come to council the following week.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment: Tipped Wage Credit
Topic2.Summary: Speakers including labor organizers, tipped workers, restaurant owners, and a clinic employee debated a proposed freeze or increase in the tip credit. Labor advocates warned of income losses and wage theft, while restaurant voices cited slow sales and rising costs. Several speakers suggested a vacancy tax or other business support instead.

Topic3.Title: Open Comment: Open Space Sales Tax Ballot Measure
Topic3.Summary: A resident whose in-laws campaigned for the 1967 open space sales tax urged council not to advance a ballot measure that would change the dedicated open space tax. She emphasized protecting public lands permanently.

Topic4.Title: Arts Week Declaration
Topic4.Summary: Council Member Benjamin presented a declaration for Boulder Arts Week, April 3 through April 12, 2026, highlighting the creative sector's economic impact and the new Boulder Arts Blueprint. Dr. Nicholas Felder, the 2026 Bright Futures Award recipient, accepted the declaration and spoke about art's role in community.

Topic5.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic5.Summary: Council approved items 4A through 4Q on the consent agenda, including a 10-year water lease with the Town of Erie, which staff said would not jeopardize local supply during drought watch. Council Member Adams voted no on the Area III service expansion framework item. Staff committed to follow up on timing of the battery storage sales tax change.

Topic6.Title: Call-Up Check-Ins
Topic6.Summary: Council reviewed items 5A through 5D, including a synagogue site review amendment, a water tap request in Area III, a student housing site review at 28th Street and College Avenue, and a landmark alteration in Mapleton Hill. A motion to call up the student housing project for Design Advisory Board referral was withdrawn after staff said DAB had already reviewed it unanimously.

Topic7.Title: Public Hearing: Festival Lodging Rental Ordinance 8743
Topic7.Summary: Staff presented an ordinance creating a festival lodging license tier for properties with long-term rental licenses, with a one-year term and $75 fee, allowing tenants to participate with owner consent. Speakers included a resident opposed to Sundance-related growth, Barha representing landlords who requested a vacant-units-only option, and a housing official who supported the ordinance as written. Council discussed revenue split transparency, tenant protections, and application timing before adopting the ordinance 8-0.

Topic8.Title: Tip Offset Exploration and Straw Polls
Topic8.Summary: Staff presented options for modifying the tip offset under newly granted local authority, ranging from status quo to a maximized offset that would cut tipped base wages. Council Member Benjamin proposed freezing the tipped base wage at $13.80 with a January 2029 sunset. In straw polls, option three was removed, while status quo, 2A, 2B, and the Benjamin proposal stayed on the table. Council directed staff to return on timing and data availability through CAC, with a June 18 hearing under reconsideration.
